This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It ends
with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. The full explanations,
examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary digital-media raster-image vector-graphics multimedia elemental-tetrad mechanics aesthetics player-experience asset production-pipeline pre-production >}}

## 1.1 What digital media are

- **Digital media** = content stored as numbers.
- Six types in games: text, images, audio, video, animation, interactive media.
- Several types together = **multimedia**.
- Games keep media in small, compressed files (PNG, JPEG, Ogg, MP3, MP4).
- **Raster image**: a grid of pixels, blocky when enlarged (photos, paintings).
- **Vector graphics**: shapes, sharp at any size (logos, icons, buttons).

![Raster (left) and vector (right).](images/raster-vector.png){width=80%}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Raster or vector?"}
On a lab computer, draw a circle in **Paint** and zoom to 800 %. Then insert a
circle shape in **PowerPoint** and zoom in. What do you see at the edges? Which
tool is raster and which is vector?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Media as numbers"}
Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="text|animation"}
A cut-scene between two levels.
:   video

The game logo for a tiny icon and a big poster.
:   vector

A painted forest background with soft light.
:   raster

The pause button for phones of many sizes.
:   vector

Several media types together in one work.
:   multimedia
:::
:::

## 1.2 The game as a composite medium

- The **elemental tetrad** (Schell): **mechanics** (rules), story,
  **aesthetics** (look, sound, feel), technology (device, engine, screen).
- All four together create the **player experience**.
- Game media live mostly in story and aesthetics; technology limits them.
- Media succeed when they make the planned experience stronger.

![The elemental tetrad.](images/tetrad.png){width=62%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Aesthetics are not only graphics: sound, music and vibration are aesthetics
too.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/juice-it.html" poster="sims/juice-it.png" title="Juice It: same mechanics, different media" kind="game" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Juice It"}
Play **Juice It** for 30 seconds with all layers off. Then switch the layers
on one at a time. Choose one word for the experience at the start and one at
the end. Which layer changed it most?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The tetrad of Lantern Keeper"}
Choose the element of the tetrad. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="player experience"}
Tap to float up; collect fireflies to grow the light.
:   mechanics

The spirit must light the village lanterns before sunrise.
:   story

Warm light, soft piano, a gentle chime.
:   aesthetics

A simple light effect so old phones keep 60 fps.
:   technology

A rumble of the phone when the spirit is hit.
:   aesthetics
:::
:::

## 1.3 The creative production pipeline

- **Pre-production**: plan (idea, script, storyboard, style, time, budget).
- **Production**: make the **assets** (draw, model, compose, record, film).
- **Post-production**: finish (edit, mix, correct colours, compress, export).
- Then test in the game; testing can send work back.
- Example: the firefly chime is recorded three times, so the sound does not
  repeat exactly; a tester says it is too loud, and it goes back to mixing.
- Free lab tools: Paint, GIMP, Krita, Blender, Audacity, DaVinci Resolve.

![The creative production pipeline.](images/pipeline.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Make one small asset"}
Make a coin icon in three stages: write a one-line plan (pre-production), draw
it in Paint (production), and save it as `icon_coin_v1.png`
(post-production).
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Which stage?"}
Choose the stage of the pipeline. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="testing only"}
Writing the script of a cut-scene.
:   pre-production

Recording the voice of the hero.
:   production

Mixing the music so that voices stay clear.
:   post-production

Drawing the storyboard.
:   pre-production

Exporting the trailer as an MP4 file.
:   post-production
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Lantern Keeper's media plan {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

The *Lantern Keeper* team must plan its media. The game needs a 2-minute music
loop, a firefly chime with three variations, a logo for the store page, a
painted forest background and a 30-second trailer. The story: the spirit must
light the village lanterns before sunrise. The team works in the order of the
pipeline. First play the game, and switch each element of the tetrad off once.

{{< sim file="sims/lantern-keeper.html" poster="sims/lantern-keeper.png" title="Lantern Keeper: switch the tetrad on and off" kind="game" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Planning the media (harder)"}
Lantern Keeper's plan: a 2-minute music loop, a firefly chime with three
variations, a logo for the store, a painted forest background, a 30-second
trailer; the story: light the village lanterns before sunrise. Choose the
right answer.

::: {.match extra="raster|pre-production|mechanics"}
"Light the lanterns before sunrise": which element of the tetrad?
:   story

Why the chime has three variations instead of one.
:   so it does not repeat exactly

The image type for the logo, on a tiny icon and a big banner.
:   vector

The image type for the painted forest background.
:   raster

The stage in which the trailer is edited and exported.
:   post-production
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Digital media are content stored as numbers; games compress them.
- Raster = pixels; vector = shapes that stay sharp.
- Tetrad: mechanics, story, aesthetics, technology → player experience.
- Pipeline: pre-production → production → post-production → testing.
